name: find-in-page-walks-and-closes
description: Cmd+F used to be swallowed, because the stock find bar dereferences a null FindBarOwner on a chromeless window. It now opens Atrium's own bar on the /find route. Four legs in one run: the bar arrives typable without a click, typing counts the matches, Cmd+G and Cmd+Shift+G move the ordinal in both directions, and Escape takes the bar away. The count is read out of the page rather than off pixels: an ordinal is a number, and a pixel gate over a number is a gate that cannot say which way it moved.

actions.note: GATE: a committed navigation, so there is a real tab with real text to find. Same line and same reason as quit-with-tab.
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot. Without this the chord lands in Finder and everything below passes on a key that was never delivered
the bar has to build its document and take key before a keystroke can land in the field
no click first. If these keystrokes land, the bar earned key status on its own, which is the property the command bar's own scenario was written for.
example-domain.html renders the word twice. Two is what makes the walk below meaningful: with one match, next and previous both read 1 of 1 and prove nothing.

Both halves of Close() in one read. Counting .fb nodes cannot say this: Close() hides the widget rather than destroying its document, so the element is still there and the count is 1 whether the bar went away or not. Measured on the run of 2026-09-05: 1 after Escape. Visibility and focus both flip, and both are page-observable.

assertions.label: the-tab-loaded-first
assertions.note: THE POSITIVE GATE, first on purpose. It proves a tab had committed before the chord, so every count below was read off a real page rather than an empty one.

assertions.desc: Cmd+G moved to the second match
and Cmd+Shift+G moved back to the first
Escape took the bar away and gave the keyboard back

assertions.label: the-session-ended
assertions.note: The highlights go with the bar. A close that hid the widget and left the session running would leave the tab marked as searching, which is the state that makes Chrome build a FindBarController on the next insert.

The find bar's null FindBarOwner deref is browser-side, so a regression here kills the browser process and this reads 0 windows rather than a wrong number. min_area keeps the 348x52 bar itself out of the count.

assertions.desc: and the app quit through its own path, not on a signal
